metric-help-stamina: Work stops recovery. Release actions and rest for 2 seconds. Healthy full recovery with default settings: seated/crouched about 21 s, standing 42 s, walking 167 s; poor condition slows it. After exhaustion, remain still until stamina reaches 35% and lactate is below 60%. Walking allows retreat but cannot restore exhausted stamina.

metric-help-plasma: Plasma-water sub-ledger within body water; does not charge water a second time.
metric-help-oxygen: Movement and hand work share native oxygen. With air, exercise leaves a 10% floor. Recovery starts after 2 uninterrupted seconds without strong work: about 45 seconds from empty to full when healthy and stationary; walking takes four times as long. Immersion, suffocation and smoke retain their native costs.

metric-help-jump: Actual takeoff velocity multiplier applied to native jumping, not a height percentage. Low stamina, fatigue and sleep pressure preserve ordinary jumps. effect-help-norovirus: Contaminated-water exposure precedes incubation and illness. Symptoms increase water loss and impair function and recovery. Rehydrate and rest; washing does not cure infection. Timing is a game approximation; water risk is not detection of this agent.
effect-help-giardia: Contaminated food or water causes sustained diarrhea and fluid loss. Rehydrate, rest and use targeted mugwort preparations; medicine does not replace lost water.
effect-help-wound-staph: Contaminated open wounds supply exposure. Illness slows healing and impairs function. Washing and alcohol bandages reduce contamination without instantly curing an established infection. Antibiotics are not implemented.
effect-help-thirst: Water deficit begins to impair function. Drink suitable water; absorption takes time.
effect-help-dehydration: Marked deficit impairs movement and recovery; severe deficit damages health. Seek shade, rest and rehydrate.
effect-help-hypothermia: Low core temperature impairs function with cold visual feedback; severe cooling damages health. Seek shelter, dry clothing and moderate warmth.
effect-help-heat-illness: Heat stress warns at core temperature 37.5°C plus the fever setpoint offset when absorbed available water is below 800 mL. At 39.5°C it warns regardless of water. Reduce exertion, improve cooling and drink; stomach water must be absorbed first. Continuous sweating, heat balance and heat damage still follow actual temperature.
effect-help-drowsy: From 90% sleep pressure, a warning precedes involuntary eye closure. At 90/95/100%, open intervals are 60/45/25 s and full closure lasts 0.25/0.4/0.7 s. Each full closure may turn the view once by 60–180 degrees. Current pressure causes mild edge dimming and at most 15% blur; recovery clears it. Confirmed food or water grants 150 s of relief. Voluntary K rest never turns the view.
effect-help-exhaustion: Fatigue above 60% gradually reduces walking, sprint gain and work efficiency. At 80/90/100%, walking retains 95/90/85% and work retains 90/80/75%. Edge dimming reaches only 4/7/10%, without blur pulses. Sit with G and rest with K, or sleep in a bed.
effect-help-pain: Wound pain impairs actions; cleaning, bandaging, nutrition and rest support recovery.
effect-help-blood-loss: Reduced blood volume impairs perfusion and endurance; severe loss damages health. Hold pressure on one wound and apply bandages.
effect-help-water-enteric: Illness follows contaminated-water exposure and incubation. Symptoms increase water loss and impair function. Drink clean water and rest; washing does not cure it.
effect-help-wound-local: Contaminated wounds supply exposure. Illness slows healing and impairs function. Clean water and alcohol bandages reduce contamination; established infection is not instantly cured.
effect-help-anemia: A depleted known iron reserve reduces endurance. This nutritional trend is not a blood test; bleeding is tracked separately.
effect-help-scurvy: Sustained vitamin C deficiency slows repair and worsens existing wound bleeding; it creates no spontaneous wound.
effect-help-thiamine-deficiency: Sustained B1 deficiency increases fatigue accumulation and slows fatigue recovery.
effect-help-b6-deficiency: Sustained B6 deficiency increases fatigue burden. Consistent dietary intake is needed; one meal is not an instant cure.
effect-help-night-vision: Sustained vitamin A deficiency mildly darkens night vision; this is a gameplay approximation.
effect-help-bone-weakness: A depleted known calcium reserve reduces bone support and maximum health. Ordinary dietary deficiency does not reduce jump height.
effect-help-clotting-deficiency: Sustained vitamin K deficiency worsens existing wound bleeding. Pressure and bandages still help.
effect-help-repair-deficiency: Sustained protein or zinc deficiency slows recovery. Varied food and rest support repair.
effect-help-inflammation: Sustained essential-fatty-acid deficiency raises a bounded inflammation trend and slows recovery without a second health charge.
effect-help-well-nourished: Known reserves and current body condition support a modest recovery bonus; excess intake cannot stack it indefinitely.
effect-help-well-rested: Low fatigue, low sleep pressure and good condition support stamina and fatigue recovery without waiving activity costs.

handbook-start-title: 01 Seraph: Survival Simulation · Your first day
handbook-start-text:
Using this guide

Seraph (SLSS) connects food, short-term endurance, sleep, wounds, hygiene and the environment. Secure water, food and shelter first; improve long-term nutrition afterwards. You do not need to fill every meter. This guide covers implemented gameplay; server configuration can change defaults. It is a game guide, not medical advice.

Six priorities for your first day

1. Press C and check water, health, core temperature, sleep pressure and stamina. Deal with active bleeding, overheating or hypothermia before gathering. Read warning tooltips and the corresponding panel together.

2. Find water and identify fresh versus salt water, turbidity and pathogens. Plan boiling or distillation. A source classification is not a safety certificate; an initially unknown reading is not clean water.

3. Keep identifiable food available. Food enters the stomach before digestion and absorption; drinking does not instantly restore blood. Rehydrate in portions and watch the reserve.

4. Release your controls between mining, sprinting and fighting. Passive stamina recovery starts after 2 continuous real seconds of rest. Sitting is usually faster. After exhaustion, stop moving and release the tool trigger.

5. Avoid sewage and smoke. Obtain bandages and a sheltered sleeping place. Stop bleeding before sleeping; sleep does not cancel ongoing injury.

6. Use a bed when sleepy. K closes your eyes without advancing time and cannot replace bed sleep indefinitely. On waking, check water, wounds, bowel load and supplies.

What to learn next

This category contains 18 chapters. Start with interface and units, drinking, endurance, sleep and first aid. Then build filters, wells, a bathtub and a latrine; learn distillation, fertilizer and soap once settled. Each chapter links to related topics. Search H for Seraph, an item name or a symptom.

Three distinctions that matter

Stamina covers short bursts, fatigue reflects sustained work, and sleep pressure reflects time awake. Blood toxicity, a named infection and inhaled smoke dose are also different problems requiring different responses.

handbook-interface-text:
Everyday controls

C opens native character panels; H opens the survival handbook; G sits using the native action. K toggles grounded closed-eye rest. Hold P to apply pressure to a bleeding wound. Shift+V starts ground defecation; pressing again cancels. Shift+right mouse performs contextual water, cleaning or latrine actions. Rebound keys and conflicts with other mods are resolved in your control settings.

Read the unit first

Water 0–8000 g is an available hydration reserve, not total body water. Blood is in L, gut contents in g, fat and muscle in kg. Nutrient and burden scores of 0–100 are not milligrams. Movement 85% is relative capability, not success chance. kcal/game hour is a rate, not food already consumed. Core and skin temperatures are separate readings.

Reading ▲, ▼ and —

A neutral white ▲ beside a meter or number means a recent measured increase; ▼ means decrease; — means no significant observed change or insufficient samples. Native bars retain their appearance and numbers do not change red or blue. These symbols describe recent observations, not predictions or health judgments: rising water and rising sleep pressure mean different things. Entering a world, respawning or losing fresh snapshots restarts sampling; tiny changes can remain a line.

Which panel to open

Body and digestion show wounds, bleeding and gut load. Environment shows air, water and pollution. Immunity shows named diseases and stages. Body functions show practical capabilities. Nutrition shows reserves and deficiencies. Thermoregulation shows heat balance and clothing. Use a panel title's pin to keep needed readings visible after closing C.

Time and progress

Game hours are normalized to a 24-hour day; day length changes the corresponding real waiting time. Physiology follows the server calendar, with no offline or paused catch-up. Short interactions and exertion costs use real seconds. Action rings are displays: the server decides completion and rewards, and pending confirmation is capped at 98%. Movement, releasing controls or losing permission can cancel. Pressure has an activity ring and elapsed duration, never a permanent completion percentage.

Missing or frozen readings

Check HUD visibility, whether your character is alive and whether server synchronization is valid. Unknown is not zero. A paused display does not imply ongoing recovery. Wait for synchronization after reconnecting; inspect versions and logs if it persists rather than repeatedly forcing interactions.

handbook-water-text:
Drinking waste burden

Water quality names known pathogens and shows game exposure intensity, not organism counts or infection probability. Potential blood waste is turbidity times 1000 mL per litre: default pond water carries 400 mL/L, about 100 mL in a 250 mL serving. This budget enters blood as stomach water is absorbed, not as a fixed toxicity percentage. Filtering lowers impurities and this burden; boiling mainly handles pathogens and leaves existing impurities.

Before drinking

Find reachable water or a drinkable native container. Read source type, salt, turbidity, pathogens and chemical pollution separately. Surface freshwater distinguishes ponds, lakes and rivers; Rivers adds its dedicated river classification when available. Cached information can arrive after targeting: wait for it, because unknown does not mean uncontaminated.

Drinking from the ground

1. Point at water within 6 blocks with an empty hand or without an item that takes priority.

2. Stand still on the bank and hold Shift+right mouse for about 3 real seconds. Do not move or swim. Washable produce takes priority, so switch to an empty hand if necessary.

3. Wait for server confirmation of a serving, normally 0.25 L. Watch stomach liquid and then available water; absorption is not instant.

Containers retain native drinking controls. Cancellation or a ring waiting at 98% is not a completed drink. Check distance, posture, cooldown and synchronization.

Clear-looking water can still be unsafe

Default pond/lake/river freshwater has roughly 40%/15%/10% turbidity and normalized background shigella exposure intensity of 0.5/0.35/0.2 per L. These are gameplay exposure values, not organism counts or laboratory concentrations. A 0.25 L pond-water drink contributes in proportion to its volume. Repeated raw-water drinking accumulates exposure and may cause infection; exposure intensity is not infection probability. Local pollution can change quality; flowing water is not guaranteed sterile. Ordinary filtering or boiling does not desalinate seawater, and dilution does not disinfect it.

Choose the treatment for the problem

Settle or filter suspended dirt, sufficiently heat water for pathogens, and distil it to remove salt. Filter media reduce turbidity and some contamination but still mark output unverified. Boiling retains salt and does not promise removal of every chemical. Read the current container metadata rather than its generic item name.

Recovering from dehydration

Leave heat and heavy work, drink safe portions, allow absorption and check electrolytes and disease. Default dehydration stages begin at 2000/1500/1000/500/0 g available water. Filling the stomach cannot restore every function immediately. Diarrhea, sweating and bleeding increase needs. If hydration improves but blood remains low, address blood loss instead of drinking indefinitely.

Water already stored before upgrading

Recognizable old default surface water and one-pass filtered water convert automatically, once. Unknown, mixed, polluted or custom legacy water retains its original values and shows a replacement warning; old high readings are not the new background. Drain and refill the container, tub or fixture. Actual boiling clears microbial exposure and the compatibility warning, but does not remove salt or guarantee removal of all chemical contamination.

handbook-filter-text:
Materials and placement

Search H for the filter and drain recipes. The filter uses knife, 1 log and axe in a row; the drain uses 2 logs instead, retaining tools. Prepare 1 gravel or 4 stones, 2 charcoal, 1 linen and a water container. Place the half-height filter directly above the drain's receiving basin, not above an arbitrary spout.

Set up the flow

1. Plan the receiver and height first. Place the drain, then its filter above the basin.

2. Add gravel/stones, then charcoal, then linen. Confirm the complete layer state in the block information.

3. Add water with a container. Put another basin, open wooden barrel or bucket under the outlet. Outlets search down at most 1 block; half-step chains can connect multiple stages.

4. Leave receiver capacity. Check upstream volume falling and downstream volume and quality changing. An absent or full receiver spills water; it is not stored invisibly.

Capacity and treatment

The reservoir holds 10 L and a complete media set processes a nominal 80 L. Default layered flow is about 1.5 L per normal-calendar real minute. A drain alone passes about 6 L/min without cloth or 3 L/min with cloth. Calendar speed and configuration affect real waiting time. Loaded blocks and available user permissions are required; unattended offline production is not guaranteed.

Complete media leave turbidity ×0.08, pathogens ×0.15 and chemical pollution ×0.25, with salt unchanged. These are remaining fractions, not sterile distilled water. Treat the result further when needed.

Replacing media and fixing failures

An empty bucket can recover retained water. Empty the vessel before Shift+empty hand resets media; unused media are returned and used media are discarded. If flow stops, check layer order, remaining media, outlet height, receiver capacity, land claims and loaded chunks. Repeated rebuilding will not fix a misplaced receiving container.

handbook-wells-text:
A wellhead alone is not an infinite source

Prepare SLSS well walls, a wellhead and a wooden bucket. Build a continuous vertical wall column over a foundation with a solid upper face and cap it with the wellhead; validation checks up to 64 layers. Depth, aquifer inflow and stored water are distinct. Read prospecting and block information rather than assuming a deep well always has abundant water.

Lift water

1. Right-click the wellhead with a native wooden bucket to lower it.

2. Hold Shift+right mouse to raise it, keeping distance, permission and the structure valid.

3. Right-click to retrieve the bucket and check its actual contents. If it fails, inspect storage, bucket state, continuous walls and foundation before repeating clicks.

Diagnosing failures

Check the well walls, foundation, groundwater supply, bucket and claim permissions.

Storage, recharge and water quality

A well stores water separately from the regional groundwater supply. Drawing removes stored well water first; groundwater then replenishes it gradually. Wells in the same region share that supply. Watch stored volume, capacity and inflow before increasing daily use. Empty storage space does not guarantee that groundwater can fill it immediately.

Check the quality of each bucket. A well head does not disinfect water. Filter sediment, heat water to address pathogens and distil saline water when freshwater is needed. Keep treated drinking water separate from untreated washing water.

handbook-distillation-title: 06 Seraph: Distilled water, sea salt and cured meat
handbook-distillation-text:
Where do the devices come from?

The boiler and condenser are native Vintage Story 1.22.7 distillation equipment; no additional mod is required. Use their own H entries for crafting, connections, heating and cooling. This chapter explains Seraph water metadata and salt conservation alongside those native rules.

Collect distilled water

1. Assemble the native boiler, condenser and receiver correctly, add water and provide sustained heat.

2. Water must actually reach at least 100°C and the native setup must be operational. A flame or the temperature alone does not prove the connections and receiver are correct.

3. The output remains the native water item with distilled-water metadata. Inspect container quality information. Salt remains on the boiler side; an unchanged generic item name does not mean distillation failed.

Make sea salt

Evaporation or distillation removes water and concentrates salt. Above the liquid salt capacity of 400 g/L, excess salt becomes residue. Firepit evaporation also retains salt. Each SLSS sea-salt item represents 20 g. Collect from a boiler with an empty hand, or from a firepit with Shift+empty hand. Fractions below one item persist. Boiling alone does not collect freshwater: you must capture condensed water for the distilled product.

Cure meat with sea salt

1. Put 2 sea-salt items and 1 supported raw meat in a native barrel.

2. Confirm the barrel recipe preview, then seal for 480 game hours: 20 normalized days, not 20 minutes.

3. Recipes cover native raw red meat, poultry, bushmeat and fish. The corresponding native cured meat carries 40 g salt. Unknown modded meats are not automatically supported.

Troubleshooting

No distillate: check native temperature, connections, receiver space, cooling and permissions. No salt: check input salinity, remaining liquid and whether residue reaches 20 g. No curing preview: verify SLSS sea salt, supported raw meat and quantities before sealing.

handbook-food-title: 07 Seraph: Food, digestion and long-term nutrition
handbook-food-text:
Stomach contents are not reserves

Food occupies the stomach before digestion supplies water, energy and nutrients. A full stomach does not mean glycogen is restored. kcal/game hour is current expenditure, not calories just eaten. Body and digestion show stomach composition, liquid and bowel contents; nutrition shows energy and micronutrient reserves.

A practical eating routine

1. Read known mass, energy, water and nutrients in food tooltips. Rotate reliable grains, produce and meat rather than eating a single food indefinitely.

2. Eat a portion and allow digestion. Leave stomach room for water before travel or work. The default digestion baseline is about 1667 g/game hour; disease and body state affect results.

3. Consider both immediate supplies and long-term reserves. Protein, water and payable energy limit repair. Vitamins and minerals recover over time; a meal does not instantly remove a chronic deficiency.

4. Hold supported washable produce and Shift+right-click suitable water. Confirm that the action says food washing. Dirty washing water can add contamination; washing does not replace cooking or preservation.

Full but still weak?

Incomplete digestion, dehydration, low blood, named disease, deficiency burdens and injuries can all limit capability. Each actual 1 HP healed costs about 2 g protein and 10 kcal; insufficient resources prevent free repair. Blood regeneration is separate and does not instantly complete after eating meat.

Understanding calories

Sustained heavy activity contributes 450 kcal/game hour; light crafting or bow work contributes 160. Total expenditure also includes basal needs, movement, cold response and repair. Intermittent breaking is averaged over accepted working time. A stable short-window reading does not mean flat fees, and low efficiency does not multiply the same per-time labor fee again.

Modded food and unknown data

Recognized native or nutrition metadata use the actual food bridge. Unknown saturation does not fabricate exact mass, vitamins or calories by default. Servers may enable estimates, but estimates are not verified recipes. Check compatibility and report the item code rather than assuming an unknown food treats a particular deficiency.

Sourced composition and category fallback

Identified ingredients use composition per 100 g and a game portion. Calcium, iron and vitamins are converted from mg or μg to reserve input; composition is sourced, but game item mass remains an estimate. Unverified mixed, cured, smoked or cooked foods do not inherit raw-food precision. Other foods with valid native nutrition use category fallback, not a verified recipe. Foods without valid metadata or with custom eating interfaces need separate checks.

Ketosis
Builds gradually during sustained low glycogen and fat-dominant fuel use. Brief fat use has no immediate penalty. Symptoms begin at 25%, with another warning at 60%. Work and stamina recovery remain at least 85% and share the strongest load limit. Absorbed carbohydrate and a lower fat fuel share allow gradual recovery. This is not a ketoacidosis diagnosis. Rise time constant: 6 h; clearance: 2 h. Offline time and pauses do not advance it.
handbook-stamina-text:
Different loads, different roles

Stamina covers bursts, fatigue reduces sustained efficiency, sleep pressure affects alertness, and lactate accumulates during strong exertion. For the same capability, the strongest of these load penalties applies instead of multiplying them together. Injury, oxygen and fuel remain independent restrictions. Low stamina, ordinary fatigue and sleep pressure alone no longer reduce jump height; exhaustion and leg injuries still can restrict actions.

Healthy costs in real time

Sprinting costs 1.5% stamina/second; mining, logging, ignition and heavy tools 1.8%/second; accepted attacks 5% each; actual jumps 2% each; bow and light crafting 0.64%/second; climbing 1.2%/second. Swimming adds no separate stamina fee but blocks passive recovery. Mounted costs require actual control, not merely riding as a passenger. These already include the ×0.8 cost adjustment.

Recover correctly

1. Release tools, sprint and other strong actions for at least 2 continuous real seconds.

2. Healthy recovery is 4.8 percentage points/second seated, 2.4 standing or 0.6 walking, including ×1.2 recovery. Injury and recovery support can reduce it.

3. Empty stamina or full lactate capacity latches exhaustion. Release the triggering action and rest stationary until stamina reaches at least 35% and lactate falls below 60% capacity. Walking while holding the tool cannot unlock it.

Gradual penalties

At stamina 35/20/10/5/0%, labor retains 100/95/70/45/25% and extra sprint gain retains 100/90/80/70/60%. At lactate 50/80/90/100% capacity, both retain 100/85/65/25%. Lower efficiency does not raise the fee per second. Warnings occur once per worsening stage at stamina 20/5% and lactate 80/95%; full exhaustion has one separate notice. The C body-functions page shows the actual jump velocity multiplier: 100% for ordinary jumps, 0% when exhaustion or severe leg injury blocks takeoff, and the applied reduction for other leg injuries. Fatigue starts affecting performance above 60%, reaching walking ×0.85 and extra sprint/labor ×0.75 at 100%. Sleep pressure starts above 70%, reaching extra sprint/labor ×0.85 at 100% without directly reducing walking. Anchors interpolate linearly. Sprint limits apply only to the native extra sprint benefit, not the whole movement speed again.

When work will not restart

Escape walking remains available, as do drinking, bathing, bandaging, pressure and rest. Read the red reason and body functions rather than repeatedly restarting. Oxygen uses the native reserve: exercise in air does not itself drain below 10%, while underwater has no such floor. Recovery begins after two seconds of rest. Leave smoke or drowning hazards before waiting for stamina.

handbook-sleep-title: 09 Seraph: Beds, closed-eye rest and daily rhythm
handbook-sleep-text:
Beds, sitting and K do different jobs

Bed sleep can accelerate time under native rules and restores sleep pressure and fatigue. G sitting suits short breaks. K closes the eyes without accelerating the calendar, preserving grounded posture and exit rules. Non-bed rest only lowers sleep pressure to about 50% and cannot replace daily sleep. There is no temporal-gear bed reserve or winter season-skipping system.

Prepare for the night

1. Deal with active bleeding, dangerous temperature, dehydration and smoke first. Sleep does not grant damage immunity.

2. Use a complete bed and improve shelter, temperature, ventilation and pollution. Bed and environment jointly determine quality; straw and comfortable beds are not equivalent.

3. Read the bed's current recovery preview, then use native bed controls. Native tiredness, permitted duration, storms and multiplayer conditions remain; SLSS sleep pressure does not replace the native admission threshold.

4. On waking, check actual pressure and supplies and plan the next sleep around your workday.

Can seven hours be enough?

Default awake sleep pressure rises 4 points/game hour. Beds restore 25 points/hour × shared quality, including the bed-only multiplier of 2. Fatigue restores 12.5 points/hour × quality, separately. At 45% quality, seven hours restore about 78.75 sleep-pressure points; seventeen awake hours add about 68. Configuration and state affect the result, so use the preview instead of the old roughly 40-point expectation.

Using and leaving K rest

Press K while safely grounded and still. The three native meters and numbers remain readable with closed eyes. K again, movement or injury can end rest. Riding, swimming, flying and climbing are not normal ground rest. Voluntary K rest never triggers random turning and low pressure alone does not force you out.

High-pressure warnings

Involuntary closures begin at 90%. At 90/95/100%, open-eye intervals are about 60/45/25 real seconds, with full closure held 0.25/0.4/0.7 seconds and a 1.5-second warning. Each full closure can turn view once by 60°–180°, subject to menu protections and settings. Blur and dimming fade with current load rather than retaining historical maximum pressure. Temporary adrenaline alertness ends by returning to the current burden.

handbook-firstaid-text:
First steps after injury

1. Escape the attacker, heat or fall hazard. Check wounds, bleeding and blood volume in the body panel.

2. Without a bandage, hold P to press the largest bleeding wound. Pressure reduces that wound's bleeding by about 90% only while maintained. Releasing or interrupting ends the effect. A moving activity ring never means permanent closure.

3. Apply real bandages to individual wounds. One bandage treats one wound; check other sites instead of assuming one notification stops everything.

4. Once bleeding is controlled, wash using safe water, stay clean, eat and rest. Nonbleeding wounds can still receive care.

Body washing is not wound cleaning

Read the action name and target. Body washing reduces dirt; wound cleaning treats wound contamination. The cleaning target follows context and actual need, without a manual region selector. Dirty water can contaminate wounds again. Native bandages, alcohol dressings and recognized poultices use actual item behavior. A medicine extension API does not automatically supply unregistered medicines.

Why recovery is still slow

Stopping bleeding, closing wounds, healing HP and regenerating blood are separate processes. Each actual HP repaired costs about 2 g protein and 10 kcal plus water and sufficient recovery support. Natural clotting is slow: a game hour reduces baseline flow by about 1.5 mL/game minute. Severe wounds retain a natural-clotting floor; K rest is not a substitute for treatment.

Body regions and danger

Default base health is about 100: head and torso 20 each, limbs 15 each, with muscle affecting limits. Severe head or torso injury can kill; regional damage restricts practical actions. Uncertain hit locations can be estimates, and ordinary blunt hits do not automatically diagnose fractures. Optional Downed integration still requires real care and resources and cannot promise rescue from every death.

Adrenaline is not treatment

Qualifying trauma can trigger about 20 real seconds of alertness, with roughly 320 seconds of trigger lockout. It does not refill blood, heal or stop bleeding. When the countdown ends, actual load still governs capabilities; temporary alertness is not a reason to keep fighting while bleeding.

handbook-blood-title: 11 Seraph: Blood volume, waste and toxicity
handbook-blood-text:
Four distinct readings

Blood volume is circulating L; water is available hydration; blood waste is metabolic mL awaiting filtration; toxicity is the physiological effect relative to waste capacity. Reference blood is about 5 L by default. Waste capacity is 25% of actual blood volume: 5 L gives 1250 mL, but bleeding reduces this capacity.

Where waste goes

Paid fuel use, lactate clearance and protein repair produce waste. Default ordinary filtration is about 72 mL/game hour and transfers material into the bowel. A full bowel blocks that route; extra high-load filtration consumes electrolytes. Bowel contents can therefore rise slowly even without food currently in the stomach.

When toxicity appears

Warnings begin around 40% of waste capacity, with toxicity increasing through 40%–85%. Raw overload can exceed 100%; a full bar does not stop accumulation. Healthy players who empty their bowels and avoid prolonged severe injury or illness may rarely reach it. Symptoms depend on the long-term balance of waste production, filtration and defecation.

Respond in order

1. Check blood volume and ongoing bleeding; stop blood loss, which also shrinks waste capacity.

2. Check bowel contents and defecate when appropriate to unblock filtration.

3. Reduce sustained heavy work, obtain safe water and suitable food and allow actual filtration and recovery to proceed.

4. Follow waste, toxicity, electrolytes and bleeding over time rather than declaring recovery from one snapshot.

Different kinds of poisoning

Blood toxicity does not identify a bacterium, and smoke dose is not blood-waste capacity. Use disease stages for infection and air/dose readings for smoke. Drinking does not directly empty waste; defecation does not instantly cure infections. There is no universal detox button.

handbook-disease-title: 12 Seraph: Pathogens, insect bites and immunity
handbook-disease-text:
Exposure is not immediate disease

A pathogen needs a real source and route, followed by possible incubation, symptoms and recovery. Ordinary dust, clean food or bathing does not invent every named organism. The immunity panel's disease names, burdens and stages are more informative than one generic icon, and diseases do not share a universal cure timer.

When you see an insect or bite warning

Read the red clinical message and distinguish attachment, an actual bite and established infection. Clean appropriately before attachment matures, keep the body clean and leave sewage or insect sources. A bite does not guarantee infection every time. No immediate disease name does not rule out incubation; keep observing.

After drinking contaminated water

Stop using that source, obtain safe water and watch diarrhea, nausea, hydration and electrolytes. Incubation can initially have no obvious symptoms, so do not keep testing the source by drinking. Known food, container and source contamination affect exposure; river classification does not bypass pathogens.

When a wound is infected

Stop bleeding first, then clean using safe water and avoid recontamination. Maintain water, energy, protein and rest. Lower body dirt does not prove the wound's infection burden is gone. Severe infection combined with major dehydration, low blood or impaired consciousness can develop systemic danger; each insect bite does not immediately cause sepsis.

Immunity recovers over time

Lower effective immunity increases susceptibility to real exposures. Nutrition, sleep and recovery need time. Low immunity does not create pathogens without a source, and full immunity does not guarantee immunity to every exposure. Correct known deficiencies gradually rather than expecting one rising total score to erase all diseases.

Medicines and compatibility

Only registered, recognized medicines, dressings and care actions work. A medicine in another mod does not mean this mod supplies the same recipe. Check H and compatibility for unknown items. For reports, keep the disease name, stage, item code, time and logs; do not confuse inhaled smoke or blood toxicity with infection.

handbook-washing-title: 13 Seraph: Body washing, wound cleaning and baths
handbook-washing-text:
Choose the intended target

Read the action label. Held washable produce takes priority (about 3 real seconds, one item and 0.25 L each). Body and wound cleaning depend on actual need. Put produce away and hold Shift+right mouse on a placed water bucket with an empty hand, or stand immersed and hold Shift without mouse input for an automatic attempt. Ordinary cleaning takes about 5 real seconds. The label follows body and wound needs; it does not imply that only one manually selected region was washed.

Use a bathtub

1. Place the complete two-block tub and fill it with native liquid containers. Both halves accept water interaction.

2. Capacity is 200 L. Starting and finishing require at least 80 L at 0–45°C; success uses 20 L. Check volume, temperature and quality first.

3. Enter the tub and use the seated/Shift/G low posture required by the interaction. Remain for about 5 real seconds, keeping position, access and water valid, and wait for server confirmation.

4. Check dirt, wounds and bathwater afterwards. Refill below the start threshold and replace dirty water. A cancelled action is not a completed bath.

Using soap

Right-click the tub with SLSS soap or soap powder to add a cleaning charge, up to 5 stored charges. Actual bathing consumes charges under current rules. A tub can still be used without soap, and one bar does not permanently disinfect all water. See soapmaking for recipes; a complete herbal-soap catalog is not supplied.

Cleaning is different from drinking safety

Ordinary surface water can be used for bathing. Without soap, the cleaning residue floor is turbidity times 0.3: default pond/lake/river water leaves about 12%/4.5%/3% body dirt. Pathogen intensity no longer becomes visible dirt or makes all water 90% dirty. At the residue floor, with no body dirt or open wound that can benefit, washing will not start or consume more water. Agents still use their actual contact routes: bathing suitability does not imply raw drinking safety.

Risks after washing

Use and environment affect bathwater. Lower dirt does not mean all pathogens died; dirty water can contaminate the body or wounds again. Washing wets and chills you, so prepare dry clothing and safe warmth in cold weather. Rain and swimming also depend on water quality and are not unlimited sterile baths.

Stay clean

Dirt, sand and gravel walking, butchering and carrying manure are actual dirt sources. Washing provides subsequent protection: roughly 24 game hours at ×0.5 dirt growth, or 72 hours at ×0.2 after a bath, taking the stronger effect. This is not immunity and does not erase later direct contamination.

If washing will not start

Check whether there is dirt or a wound needing care, whether produce takes priority, the complete tub, actual 80 L minimum, successful pouring, posture and claim access. A completed body wash does not finish an established wound disease; continue the relevant care.

handbook-sanitation-text:
The icon activates at 4000/5000 g (80%); 500 g (10%) only permits voluntary defecation. Hover to see the current load. Drinking impurities enter blood during absorption and reach the bowel through filtration. Diarrhea accounts for actual lost fluid separately without draining body water twice.

When to empty your bowels

Default bowel capacity is 5000 g. Defecation becomes available at 500 g, with a warning around 4000 g. Contents include food residue, fiber and actually filtered metabolic waste; food water does not directly become fecal mass. Full bowels can also block blood-waste filtration.

Using the ground

Stand on solid support without water where output can be placed. Press Shift+V to start and remain still; holding the key is unnecessary and pressing again cancels. Duration is 2 plus the actual number of output portions in real seconds, not a fixed 5 seconds. Movement, injury or invalid conditions interrupt. Wait for server confirmation. Ground use causes substantial dirt and pollution; keep away from drinking water, living space and crops.

Build a working latrine

1. Find the SLSS latrine recipe in H and place it completely.

2. Install an actual native wooden barrel underneath. A decorative block, arbitrary chest or imaginary infinite inventory does not qualify.

3. Check capacity and claim access, then Shift+right-click the latrine to sit and start; this differs from the ground Shift+V action. Wait for completion. Success stores actual output. Latrine use still adds a little dirt; it is not sterile.

4. Empty storage regularly and wash after handling waste. A full or locked barrel does not make output vanish.

Use manure deliberately

Manure and compost use actual items and fertilizer hooks. Recognized Natural Fertilizer integration takes priority when installed. Follow item instructions for suitable farmland and observe nutrients and pollution. Excess nitrogen, phosphorus and contamination can damage soil and reduce growth. Fertility gain does not imply drinking water is unaffected.

Failures and hygiene

If the action will not complete, check the 500 g minimum, remaining still, whether you used the ground hotkey or latrine interaction, real barrel, capacity and permissions. Carrying substantial manure dirties the body; ground sewage contaminates the area. Washing afterwards does not erase pollution dumped beside a well.

handbook-thermal-title: 15 Seraph: Heat balance, cooling and cold
handbook-thermal-text:
Heat stress warns at core temperature 37.5°C plus the fever setpoint offset when absorbed available water is below 800 mL. At 39.5°C it warns regardless of water. Reduce exertion, improve cooling and drink; stomach water must be absorbed first. Continuous sweating, heat balance and heat damage still follow actual temperature.

Adaptation units

Heat adaptation shows a 0–15% increase in sweat response. Cold adaptation shows a 0–10% reduction in core-to-skin heat transfer during cold demand. These are percentage changes in those processes, not temperature or training progress. Sweating still spends water and electrolytes and has a rate cap; shivering still spends energy.

Read core, skin and net heat separately

Core temperature, skin temperature and heat change per hour are different quantities. Negative net heat indicates overall cooling, but core and skin have separate heat capacities and exchange heat. Core temperature need not fall on the very next refresh. Displayed flow averages accepted settlement over a short synchronization window; one negative sample does not describe an entire interval.

When overheating

1. Stop strong work, leave fires and hot exposure and find cooler ventilated space.

2. Reduce excessive insulation where appropriate and obtain safe water. Sweating and evaporation cost water and electrolytes.

3. Watch core, skin and net heat over several game minutes. Sustained negative balance should reduce stored heat; skin can cool before the core does.

4. If the core keeps rising, check active tools, clothing, nearby heat and disease rather than only drinking more.

When cold

Get out of wind and rain, use dry insulating clothes, find suitable warmth and eat. Wet clothing, wind and post-bath moisture increase heat loss. Shivering and cold response consume energy; insufficient reserves impair temperature maintenance. A full stomach without leaving exposure is not safety.

Sleeping can still be dangerous

Beds provide recovery under actual environmental conditions, not immunity to temperature damage. A warning that still permits sleep is not permission to ignore danger. Bed warnings may begin below about 35.5°C or when the shared heat-stress condition is met. Correct exposure before fast-forwarding.

Clothing and compatibility

Insulation, wetness, wind and heat sources act together. Adaptation takes time rather than switching on immunity. Compatibility preserves recognized environmental sources, but unknown devices do not automatically heat or cool. For persistent negative-flow reports, record starting core and skin temperatures, environment, clothing, activity and elapsed game time to distinguish lag from settlement faults.

handbook-smoke-title: 16 Seraph: Inhaled smoke and embedded flues
handbook-smoke-text:
Check whether a concentration provider exists

With supported Real Smoke installed, Seraph samples real smoke near the eyes and integrates inhaled dose using ventilation. It does not invent exposure simply because a fire is nearby. Missing or failed sampling is unknown, not clean air that clears old dose for free. Native oxygen, coughing and optional Candela rules remain independent.

How dose grows

Concentration, breathing ventilation and actual exposure time determine dose. Stronger work raises ventilation, roughly 8–40 L/min, so identical smoke is inhaled faster. Warning begins near dose 60. From 60 to 300, respiratory capability falls gradually to about 75%. Above 300, physiological damage begins; 600 and above reaches the default maximum of about 1 HP/real minute. Dose is a game scale, not a real carbon-monoxide measurement.

Respond to warnings

Stop heavy work and leave the smoke layer for sampled clean air. The clean-air dose half-life is about 180 real seconds, so stepping outside does not instantly reset it. Check oxygen and breathing before sprinting or diving. Unknown sampling freezes dose decay; restore a reliable environment reading first.

Install an embedded flue

1. Obtain an SLSS flue and choose an existing full solid cube without a block entity. Containers and machines are not suitable hosts.

2. Keep space above and below clear. Right-click the host's bottom face from underneath to embed it. Ordinary placement as a freestanding pipe is not supported.

3. Leave the upper outlet and lower inlet open and plan the real smoke path. Breaking returns the host block and flue.

4. Supported Real Smoke allows transfer from below to above, normally up to about 32 units/second. Blocked openings or excess input still accumulate smoke. Without a concentration provider, appearance alone does not verify ventilation.

Compatibility boundaries

Successful measurement suppresses only the recognized duplicate SmokeScent firepit satiety drain, not all its mechanics. Smoke is not automatically carbon monoxide, and no universal gas-mask system is supplied. Use air readings and measured dose rather than assuming a flue makes a room safe.

handbook-soap-title: 17 Seraph: Ash, lye, soap and cleaning
handbook-soap-text:
Collect a real burn product

SLSS spawns ash at a native firepit when it transitions from burning to extinguished. Right-clicking, each frame or placing an empty firepit does not produce ash. Collect the dropped item after the burn ends; similarly named ash from another mod is not automatically a valid ingredient.

Make lye

1. Put 3 SLSS ash and 5 L native water into a sealable native barrel.

2. Confirm the lye recipe preview and seal for 24 game hours.

3. Collect 5 L lye. It is a cleaning ingredient, not drinking water; being a liquid does not make it hydration.

Make soap

1. Combine 1 native raw or rendered fat with 0.5 L SLSS lye in a barrel.

2. Confirm the recipe, then seal for 12 game hours to obtain 1 soap.

3. Look up actual soap and powder recipes in H. Right-click a bathtub with soap or soap powder to add cleaning charges, storing at most 5 and spending them on successful bathing.

A sustainable cleaning loop

Cook with fire, collect ash, seal lye, turn fat into soap, fill with clean bathwater, add soap, wash and replace dirty water while keeping the settlement clean. Ash, fat, water and time are real costs; cancellation or network replays cannot duplicate finished products.

No recipe preview?

Check item domains and quantities, other remaining liquid, a sealable barrel and actual 5 L/0.5 L amounts rather than an underfilled container. Trust the barrel preview; seal times are game hours. Additional medicinal or herbal soap variants do not mean recipes exist here. Use entries that actually exist in H.

handbook-troubleshooting-text:
An action did not finish

Read its name and red reason, then check target, distance, posture, held controls, resources, claims and server synchronization. A timed ring at 98% awaits confirmation and grants no reward yet. An endlessly moving pressure ring is intentional. Switch held items to rule out food-washing priority. Unknown water is not safe, and stale snapshots cannot keep actions running.

Recovery seems wrong

Stamina: release controls, stand still and wait 2 real seconds; exhaustion additionally needs at least 35% stamina and lactate below 60%. Sleep: use the actual bed preview; K is not accelerated sleep. Temperature: inspect core, skin and sustained net heat. Blood: stop bleeding; drinking is not instant blood creation. Disease: inspect individual stages; cleaning is not an instant cure. Toxicity: check waste, actual blood volume and bowel capacity.

Optional integrations

Rivers supplies dedicated river classification. Real Smoke supplies measured concentration and flue transfer. Recognized independent SmokeScent and Candela behavior remains. Supported vehicles, Downed, nutrition and fertilizer integrations use their actual bridges, which can fall back safely if versions or interfaces change. This mod follows its own registered features; multiple complete physiology systems may change rules in the same save.

Feature boundaries

Only registered items, symptoms and interactions listed in H are current features. An extension API, research note or old plan is not a playable item. This guide covers registered content and working paths rather than promising automatic support for every third-party food, meat, heater and liquid.

Reporting lag or crashes

Keep client/server versions, mod list, recent logs, whether breaking blocks, opening C or resting caused it, elapsed game time and reproducible steps. Check only one active version per mod ID and matching main/debug versions. Debug UI is optional client tooling, not a server prerequisite. Back up before upgrades and do not repeatedly overwrite a migrated world with older versions.

Verification boundaries

GUI scale, language, server configuration and other mods can affect behavior. Automated bridges and native Cairo checks are not live modpack FPS, multiplayer or long-save guarantees. Include actual item codes, disease names, readings and steps so unknown data can be distinguished from configuration and defects.
